title: Missed Visit Credit Basis for the Indoor Air Quality & Filtration Programs
content:
Basis on which the billing office issues a missed visit credit on a program under the Indoor Air Quality & Filtration Programs.

Where the company fails to perform a booked filter or service visit and does not rebook it inside the tier's grace period, the owner is credited. A credit is issued only when the booked visit was not performed inside the tier's grace period counted from the day the visit was booked for. The grace period is counted in business days on the office calendar, which excludes Saturdays, Sundays and the office holidays published for the year, and a visit rebooked on the final grace day is still timely. The credit is the per-visit value of the program — the annual price divided by the tier's visits for the year — multiplied by the tier's missed visit credit rate, and at the top tier that rate exceeds the per-visit value. A visit the owner postponed, and a visit the technician could not perform because the units were inaccessible, never produce a credit.

## The grace period

The day the visit was booked for is the day the count starts from, read from the visit's record on the program under its work order; the day the visit was performed, where it was performed, is read from the same record. The final grace day is the last of the tier's grace business days counted after the booked day on the office calendar. A visit performed or rebooked on or before the final grace day is timely and produces no credit; a credit arises only where the final grace day has passed and the visit was not performed inside the period.

| Day the visit was performed, relative to the booked day | Outcome |
|---|---|
| On the booked day | Timely; no credit |
| Inside the grace period, before the final grace day | Timely; no credit |
| On the final grace day | Timely; no credit |
| After the final grace day, or not performed at all once the final grace day has passed | Credit issued |

## The amount

The per-visit value is the program's annual price divided by the tier's number of visits for the year. The credit is that per-visit value multiplied by the tier's credit rate, the result rounded to the cent.

*Worked on hypothetical inputs.* A program carries an annual price of 4,800 USD at a tier with 4 visits a year; the per-visit value is 1,200 USD. At a credit rate of 100 percent the credit is 1,200.00 USD. At a credit rate of 150 percent the credit is 1,800.00 USD, which is more than the per-visit value; that is the position at the top tier, whose rate exceeds the per-visit value. At a credit rate of 0 percent the credit is 0.00 USD.

## Visits that never produce a credit

- A visit the owner postponed.
- A visit the technician could not perform because the units were inaccessible.

Neither is a missed visit for this basis, whatever the day it is eventually performed.
